Select, Textarea, and Buttons

The Simple Version

Not everything fits in an <input> tag. Sometimes you need a dropdown menu, a large text area, or different types of buttons.

  • <select> - a dropdown menu (pick one from a list).
  • <textarea> - a multi-line text box (for long messages).
  • <button> - a clickable button (more flexible than <input type="submit">)
If <input> is like a fill-in-the-blank question on an exam, then <select> is like a multiple-choice question (choose one answer from a list), and <textarea> is like an essay question (write as much as you want).

What's Really Happening

The <select> element:

<select name="county">
  <option value="">Choose a county...</option>
  <option value="nairobi">Nairobi</option>
  <option value="mombasa">Mombasa</option>
  <option value="kisumu">Kisumu</option>
</select>
  • Each <option> is one choice in the dropdown
  • value is what gets sent when the form submits (the user sees the text)
  • Add selected to an option to make it the default choice
  • Use <optgroup> to group options with a label

The <textarea> element:

<textarea name="message" rows="5" cols="40"
  placeholder="Write your message..."></textarea>
  • rows - how many lines tall (visible height)
  • cols - how many characters wide (visible width)
  • Users can type as much text as they want - it scrolls
  • Unlike <input>, default text goes between the tags, not in a value attribute

The <button> element:

<button type="submit">Send</button>
<button type="reset">Clear Form</button>
<button type="button">Do Something</button>
  • type="submit" - submits the form (default inside a form)
  • type="reset" - clears all form fields back to defaults
  • type="button" - does nothing until JavaScript tells it to

Good to know: <button> is better than <input type="submit"> because you can put HTML inside a button - images, icons, styled text. <input type="submit"> can only show plain text.
